_note: AI-drafted Call to Worship — pending Wilson's curation.

registers.label: Spare
lines: Jesus came to bring fire to the earth, and how he wished it were already kindled.
Stir the embers in us, Lord.
You brought a vine out of Egypt and planted it with your own hand.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine, that we may be saved.
So great a cloud of witnesses surrounds us; lay aside every weight.
Let us run the race set before us, eyes fixed on Jesus.
Come, and worship the pioneer of our faith.
We run, and we will not grow weary. Amen.

registers.label: Immersive
lines: Jesus says he came to cast fire on the earth — not a tame candle, but a blaze he longed to see catch and spread.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
You dug up a vine from Egypt, cleared the ground, and planted it; now you look down the long rows for the fruit of justice.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
And we are not running alone: a great cloud of witnesses fills the stands, those who ran before us and kept the faith.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
So lay down the weight that slows you, feel the fire catch, and run with your eyes fixed on Jesus, who finished the course ahead of us.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine, that we may be saved. Amen.

registers.label: Hybrid
lines: Jesus longs to set the earth on fire.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
You planted us like a vine and tend us still.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
A cloud of witnesses cheers us on the course.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine.
Lay down the weight; come run and worship.
Restore us, O God; let your face shine. Amen.
